title: Identifying Emotional States using Keystroke Dynamics
abstract: The ability to recognize emotions is critical for building intelligent computers. Emotionally-aware systems could adapt interactions based on user context, but current methods are invasive and require costly equipment. This study uses keystroke dynamics to detect emotional states through typing patterns, achieving accuracies of 77-88% for six emotional states.
problem_statement: Current emotion detection methods are invasive and require specialized equipment, limiting their practical applicability in real-world scenarios.
methodology: A field study collected keystroke data and self-reported emotional states. Keystroke features (key duration, latency) were extracted and used to train decision-tree classifiers for 15 emotional states.
dataset: Keystroke data from participants performing daily tasks, labeled with self-reported emotional states via experience-sampling questionnaires.
performance: Top results include 2-level classifiers for confidence, hesitance, nervousness, relaxation, sadness, and tiredness with accuracies 77.4-87.8%. Anger and excitement showed promise with 84% accuracy.
contribution: Proposed keystroke dynamics as a non-intrusive, cost-effective method for emotion detection, demonstrating its viability in real-world HCI applications.
limitations: Limited exploration of anger and excitement; reliance on self-reported emotional states may introduce bias.
future_work: Investigate anger and excitement further, test across varying typing abilities and keyboards, and validate in real-world stressful scenarios.

title: Behavioral Biometrics in Assisted Living: A Methodology for Emotion Recognition
abstract: Behavioral biometrics aim at providing algorithms for the automatic recognition of individual behavioral traits. In ambient assisted living, they find niche applications for monitoring neurodegenerative disease patients. The paper describes a methodology for emotion recognition using facial expressions, integrating with risk-assessment frameworks for smart monitoring systems.
problem_statement: Individuals with neurodegenerative diseases require unobtrusive monitoring systems to track physical and emotional status. Current approaches lack effective emotion recognition mechanisms for integration into smart healthcare environments.
methodology: Combines computational geometry, image processing, graph theory for region detection, and neural networks for classification. Leverages Paul Ekman's facial expression theory and integrates with service-oriented architectures for real-time monitoring.
performance: Integrated into ambient assisted living systems for remote cognitive/physical status estimation of MCI and dementia patients, enabling proactive care and alert generation.
contribution: Proposes a novel methodology for emotion recognition using facial expressions, combining biometric traits with risk-assessment frameworks for smart monitoring in neurodegenerative disease management.
limitations: Relies on specific biometric traits with dynamic variability; may require calibration for diverse populations and environmental conditions.
future_work: Enhance accuracy through multimodal biometric fusion, expand to real-time emotion tracking, and validate across diverse cultural contexts.

title: Emotion Recognition through Keystroke Dynamics on Touchscreen Keyboards
abstract: Automatic emotion recognition through computers offers advantages for improving human-computer interaction. This work investigates keystroke dynamics on touchscreen keyboards, leveraging pressure and size data to enhance emotion recognition. An Android app and keyboard layout were developed, with hypotheses based on Yerkes-Dodson-Law and Flow theory. Results confirm emotions can be recognized via keystroke dynamics.
problem_statement: Improve human-computer interaction by automatically recognizing emotions through keystroke dynamics on touchscreen keyboards, addressing limitations of conventional keyboard methods.
methodology: Developed an Android app and keyboard layout to record keystroke dynamics. Hypotheses derived from Yerkes-Dodson-Law and Flow theory. Conducted a study with 152 participants, analyzing data via SPSS to validate correlations between keystroke metrics and emotional states.
dataset: Study involving 152 test persons with varying time limits (no time limit, 5 minutes, 3.5 minutes) and demographic data (age, gender, education).
evaluation_metrics: Correlation analysis between keystroke variables (speed, error rate, pressure) and emotional metrics (valence, arousal)
performance: Most hypotheses were confirmed: typing speed, error rate, and pressure correlate with emotional valence/arousal. Keystroke dynamics effectively explain and recognize emotional states under time pressure.
contribution: First application of keystroke dynamics on touchscreen keyboards for emotion recognition, integrating biometric data (pressure, size) and psychological theories (Yerkes-Dodson-Law, Flow theory).
limitations: Study limited to controlled lab environment and specific demographics (IT employees/students). Correlation does not imply causation in emotional responses.
future_work: Explore real-world applications, diverse populations, and integration with other biometric data. Investigate long-term emotional state tracking via keystroke dynamics.

title: A Review of Emotion Recognition Methods Based on Keystroke Dynamics and Mouse Movements
abstract: The paper describes an approach using standard input devices like keyboard and mouse to recognize users’ emotional states. It reviews systems focusing on data collection, feature extraction, and classifier training for emotion recognition, along with multimodal approaches.
problem_statement: Recognizing users’ emotional states using standard input devices for affective computing applications.
methodology: Analyzing keystroke dynamics and mouse movements as biometric features, including data collection, feature extraction, and classifier training for emotion detection.
dataset: Various studies with participants performing tasks (e.g., online shopping, typing exercises) to collect physiological and behavioral data under different emotional states.
performance: Effectiveness of keystroke and mouse movement analysis in detecting emotional states, with challenges in data variability and labeling.
contribution: Comprehensive review of emotion recognition methods using input devices, highlighting multimodal approaches and real-world applications.
limitations: Variability in data collection, lack of controlled emotional states, and limited sample sizes in some studies.
future_work: Exploring multimodal integration, improving data labeling, and standardizing experimental protocols for emotion recognition.

title: Human Micro-Expression: A Novel Social Behavioral Biometric for Person Identification
abstract: A novel Social Behavioral Biometric (SBB), human micro-expression, is introduced for person identification. An emotion detection model extracts emotion probability scores from Twitter writing samples, and emotion-progression features are derived from microblogs. A rank-level weighted majority voting system achieves accurate person identification on a proprietary dataset.
problem_statement: Traditional biometric methods face limitations in online social interactions. The paper addresses the need for novel SBB traits to enhance person identification using behavioral patterns from social media.
methodology: An emotion detection model extracts emotion probability scores from microblogs. Emotion-progression features are generated using dynamic time warping. Rank-level weighted majority voting fusion improves identification accuracy.
dataset: Proprietary benchmark dataset with 250 Twitter users' microblog samples.
evaluation_metrics: Accuracy comparison with existing SBB traits
performance: Achieves high recognition rates on benchmark data, outperforming original SBB traits in emotion-progression representation.
contribution: Introduces human micro-expression as a novel SBB trait. Develops emotion detection and progression feature extraction techniques for person identification.
limitations: Relies on statistical features; performance degrades with insufficient user data. Prior SBB traits are limited by count-based feature generation.
future_work: Further technical breakthroughs in emotion-progression representation and application in online biometric systems.
model_type: Machine learning with weighted majority voting fusion
